results.content: The energy return of investment (EROI) is a useful indicator of full fossil lifecycle costs. Fossil fuels create significantly more energy per unit energy invested – or in other words have much larger EROI – than most cleaner fuels such as biomass or electrolysis-derived hydrogen, where intensive processing reduces EROI (Hall et al. 2014). results.title: Glossary - IEA
results.content:
Fossil fuels
  :   Energy sources that are typically extracted from underground and which have been formed from the fossilised remains of dead plants by exposure to heat and pressure in the Earth's crust over millions of years. Fossil fuels generate greenhouse gases during their extraction, transport and combustion or oxidation. Includes coal, natural gas, oil and peat. [...] Unabated fossil fuels
  :   Fossil fuels used for energy purposes without carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS). In IEA analysis, total fossil fuel use is equal to unabated fossil fuels plus fossil fuels with CCUS plus non-energy use of fossil fuels.

  Unabated gas
  :   See unabated fossil fuels. [...] Solar photovoltaics
  :   Electricity produced from solar photovoltaic cells including utility-scale and small-scale installations. See photovoltaic.

  Solid bioenergy
  :   Includes charcoal, fuelwood, dung, agricultural residues, wood waste and other solid biogenic wastes.

  Solid biomass
  :   See solid bioenergy.

  Solid fuels
  :   Includes coal, modern solid bioenergy, traditional use of biomass and industrial and municipal wastes.
